chunks: Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkhill (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us, saying: 'Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated to us, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu 'Abd Allah, from his forefathers (peace be upon them).

He said: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) passed by a man who was raising his gaze to the sky while supplicating, so the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to him: 'Lower your gaze, for you will certainly not see Him.' And he (peace be upon him and his family) also said: 'The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) passed by a man who was raising his hands to the sky while supplicating, so the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to him: 'Restrain your hands, for you will surely not reach Him.'
ai.seo_question: What is the proper etiquette for raising eyes and hands during supplication according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), recorded by Shaykh al-Saduq in *Al-Tawhid*, clarifies the etiquette of *dua* by distinguishing between the physical act of raising hands and the spiritual focus of the gaze. It emphasizes *tawhid* by noting that since God is beyond physical sight, excessive upward gazing is unnecessary, while raising hands to a moderate level remains a valid expression of humility and supplication.
